parsed.explanation: No entry ban or enacted presentation offence is documented, but post-arrival exposure is state-driven: ~20 trans women were stopped, documented and held for background checks, within 299 documented detention decisions in 2025, systematic privacy attacks, and raids framed around protecting children. State framing presents LGBT people as threats to family and children, no anti-discrimination protection exists, and complaints/investigation are ineffective. Custody uses registered-sex segregation, isolation, strip searches and restricted care, culminating in a trans prisoner's death without prompt investigation. Three hate killings were recorded in 2025. These combined patterns place the regime below unremedied exclusion at 0.35, above explicit imprisonment/extortion regimes at 0.25.

entry_documents.exposure: General original-photo-ID rule at holiday transit checkpoints with fines and detention warnings; police ID checks are documented mechanism initiating contact with trans women.
entry_documents.protection: No visa, entry or border condition applying to LGBTQ travellers as such is documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Document checks after arrival led to station detention and recording, even before any new law passed.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: August 2025 group detention of about 20 trans women for general information gathering; 299 detention decisions in 2025, 43 off-record; prisons use segregation/isolation, arbitrary strip searches, restricted healthcare and registered-sex placement, including a trans man in a women's prison.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Complaints are described as ineffective and capable of leading to further violence; no staff policy or training was documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Police detention can connect to documented prison practices; a 2025 trans prisoner death was followed by delayed medical response, investigators arriving two days later and no witness statements.

care_services.exposure: Hormone therapy is not covered by government healthcare and must be arranged and paid for privately; prisoners in isolation have restricted healthcare.
care_services.protection: Private arrangement is possible, but no documented visitor-cover protection. Surgery availability is resident-facing and not counted as a visitor protection.
care_services.interaction: Medication continuity depends on private payment and access; delayed medical response is documented in the custody death.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Government repeatedly frames LGBT people as a threat to children, family and public morals; draft package reported as effectively criminalising LGBT people; September 2026 raids placed 162 suspects, 9 associations and 13 businesses under investigation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: A proposed 1-3 year advocacy offence was not included in the 2026 judicial package; discriminatory provisions were also removed from the 12th judicial package.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing legitimises stigmatisation, police documentation and exclusionary demonstrations, while activists report detention asymmetry as evidence of official hate policy.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: A trans woman knifed in August 2024 saw the perpetrator released and herself referred for arrest; six deaths linked to anti-LGBTQ violence were reported in 2025, three classified as hate killings, with trans people disproportionately affected.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No effective police protection or prosecution remedy is documented for these cases.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street violence combined with arrest/referral of the victim increases exposure if outed and deters reporting.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No comprehensive anti-discrimination law or direct gender-identity protection; regional commission found protection insufficient; remedies for discrimination remain pending since 2023.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Not documented as effective. Whether the draft package has been enacted and whether the Article 5 challenge produced an outcome are unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of recourse means police detentions, custody harms and violence have no documented corrective route; airport screening and short-term police-holding conditions are not documented.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar recurring police raids/detentions, birth/registered-sex custody harms and ineffective complaints. This case is higher because no enacted presentation offence, short jail sentences or extortion are documented, and many detentions ended in release after documentation.

Similar routine police stops and documentation without effective discipline. This case is lower because 299 annual detention decisions, hate killings, state child-protection raids and a custody death with failed investigation show broader, more severe targeting than ferry-terminal extortion alone.

This case is higher than severe-risk regimes with presentation criminalisation, regular convictions, imprisonment and documented sexual assault in men's facilities. Here imprisonment for presentation and routine custodial sexual violence are not documented, and the draft criminalisation remains unresolved.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines formal entry neutrality with intensive post-arrival police documentation, escalating detention counts, state threat framing, hate violence and adverse police response, and unremedied registered-sex custody with isolation and a death lacking prompt investigation. Documentary checks are the bridge from ordinary travel to detention and recording. No bathroom rule, airport practice, enacted presentation offence or effective remedy is documented, limiting the rating against the 0.25 tier, but multiple current state-driven exposures and impunity prevent a 0.35 rating.
